correctness.rationale: For each integer n>=2, exact state counts give the rational recurrence. An exact one-pair survival identity telescopes the first factorial moment to 3n/(4n²−1) minus a positive sum. Marked two-pair survival probability is universally at most ((m−1)/m)^4 by a strictly positive integer polynomial, yielding E[(f_m)_2] <= m^4/n². A harmonic summation proves 0<=3n/(4n²−1)−p_n<=12H_(n−1)/n² and n*p_n -> 3/4. Finite exact labeled-vertex and reduced-state checks, plus independent symbolic polynomial factorization, validate critical calculations; finite tests are not used as the asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: In this dense regular family greedy maximal matchings can miss optimality by only one edge, so usual approximation ratios conceal the nontrivial reliability of the algorithm. The probability of the sole possible failure is a natural rare-event invariant; the 3/4 constant differs from the unbiased-pair 1/2 constant and the formula includes computable finite probabilities and quantitative error. It is not a generic ratio corollary, arbitrary parameter slice, or a table recomputation.
